latest_apis.rationale: Built squarely on the current stable release (1.20.3, Oct 2026) with current-generation APIs throughout; the misses are the documented 404.tsx/status(404) conventions and useNavigate for client-side navigation, not legacy-era APIs. Note Qwik 2.0 is only at rc.4, so 1.20.x is the right stable target.

app/src/routes/index.tsx:31-33 — URLSearchParams to build filter URLs; app/src/lib/data.ts:336-346 — parseHomeQuery reads url.searchParams off a platform URL
app/src/routes/index.tsx:39-118 — native form elements (input[type=search], select, option) instead of any UI library

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first — fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, native forms and tables, CSS custom properties — with no polyfills or hand-rolled replacements. The small gaps (regex URL parsing, no fetch timeouts) keep it short of exemplary.

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and largely current: no runtime deps at all and the framework toolchain is at the latest stable. Two unused starter leftovers (undici, typescript-plugin-css-modules) and a dated pinned typescript are the only blemishes.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:1-339 — all API access, caching, humanization and query parsing live behind this single module with exported types (HomeEntry, MoveRow, SpeciesCard), so an API or caching change touches one file

app/src/root.tsx, app/src/entry.ssr.tsx:24-28, app/src/entry.preview.tsx, app/src/components/router-head/router-head.tsx — starter boilerplate kept unmodified (lang='en' via containerAttributes), so a regenerate/upgrade diff stays clean
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:64-73 — loader returns a discriminated {notFound} union that components narrow, not string checks
app/src/lib/data.ts:44-50 — TypeOption.record: any / record: any used throughout; PokeAPI responses enter untyped
app/src/routes/index.tsx:64-103 — three copies of window.history.replaceState inline in handlers duplicate URL-sync logic instead of one helper or the router
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:414-417 — full page reload (window.location.assign) on game change fights the framework's client-side router
churn_resistance.rationale: A framework or upstream-API change would land in the single data module plus route loaders, and the untouched starter files mean new releases diff cleanly. The router-bypassing navigation and pervasive `any` at the PokeAPI boundary are the places churn will hurt.

findings.issue: Not-found is handled by returning {notFound:true} and a [...catchall] route instead of the documented conventions: status(404) inside routeLoader$ and a root 404.tsx. The app therefore serves HTTP 200 for missing resources, and the spec explicitly encouraged a 404 status where the architecture allows — it does.
findings.suggestion: Call status(404) from RequestEvent in each loader when the resource is missing, add src/routes/404.tsx per qwik.dev/docs/advanced/routing, and drop the catchall.

findings.issue: fetchJson caches the promise for every URL unconditionally, so a transient network error or 5xx caches `null` for the lifetime of the server process; the spec treats the API as live data that can change.
findings.suggestion: Only cache successful responses (and 404s if desired); on !response.ok or a thrown error, delete the cache entry so the next request retries.

findings.issue: Changing the game select does window.location.assign, a full document reload that discards Qwik's resumability and SPA navigation, when the router already re-runs the routeLoader on a query-param change.
findings.suggestion: Use useNavigate() (or go with the ?game= URL) so the change is a client-side navigation that re-runs usePokemonData.

findings.issue: Filter state is synced to the URL with three inline copies of window.history.replaceState, bypassing the framework's router; back/forward won't restore filter state and future router changes to URL ownership could conflict.
findings.suggestion: Extract one setFiltersUrl(params) helper, or drive the query through the router (useNavigate/useLocation) so URL state has a single owner.

findings.issue: Unused starter leftovers: typescript-plugin-css-modules ('latest' — an unpinned range) while the app uses plain global.css, and undici '*' which is never imported; tsconfig.json's own comment says to remove both when CSS modules aren't used.
findings.suggestion: Delete undici and typescript-plugin-css-modules and the tsconfig plugins line.

findings.issue: typescript is pinned at 5.4.5 (March 2024), roughly a year and a half behind current 5.9.x; this delays catching upstream type regressions.
findings.suggestion: Bump to a current ^5.8/^5.9 range and let the lockfile pin it.

findings.issue: All PokeAPI records are typed `any` (TypeOption.record, englishName(record), etc.), so API shape changes surface as silent undefined at runtime rather than compile errors, despite well-typed outputs downstream.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API shapes actually consumed (names, flavor_text_entries, types, moves, damage_relations) at the data-layer boundary.

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no AbortController or timeout; a slow upstream request can hold the SSR stream open indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add AbortSignal.timeout(...) to the fetch call so a stuck upstream fails fast and the cache can retry.

findings.issue: npm start serves the production build with `vite preview`, which Qwik positions as local preview rather than a deploy adapter — fine for this harness, but a real deployment target change touches config only.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep; when a real target is chosen, add a qwik-city server adapter (e.g. express/cloudflare) — the data layer and routes need no changes.

summary: This is a current-generation Qwik City app built on the latest stable release (1.20.3, Oct 2026) with essentially untouched starter scaffolding, current APIs (routeLoader$, useSignal/useComputed$, DocumentHead resolveValue) and every API access centralized in one typed module with zero runtime dependencies. It will age well in most respects; the risks are the places it steps around the framework (manual history/location manipulation, the undocumented-style notFound unions instead of status(404)/404.tsx) and permanently-cached failed fetches. With `any`-typed PokeAPI records at the boundary, upstream API changes would surface as runtime bugs rather than compile errors.
